utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: The witness has consistently stated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did he tell us today about -- about -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: He can't remember. And he said today, when I asked him specifically: "I want to ask you specifically whether you recall seeing Mr. Haradinaj being present during the course of that incident. "I don't recall. A long time has passed. I don't know. I'm not certain."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And that's precisely the part that my learned friend has just identified for you. What he tries to do is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... what -- what -- where on the transcript is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I don't have a page reference, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I'm just got -- I have got an unpaginated version, but that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because Mr. Emmerson referred us to page 39, and we've been given a document that starts at page 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I don't think there's any dispute about what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can get copies printed out for Your Honours. The question, I'll read it again: "I want to ask you specifically whether you recall seeing Mr. Haradinaj being present during the course of that incident. ... Mr. Haradinaj, I mean Ramush Haradinaj." This is the ear-cutting incident. "A. I don't recall. A long time has passed. I don't know. I'm not certain." The point I was trying to drive home to Your Honours is that in the passage which you do have the transcript of he goes on to say that on the occasion (redacted) --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... and when -- what is the reference in this transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You'll find that, Your Honours, at transcript page 50 -- sorry. I'm so sorry. 56. On the first occasion that you saw -- line 3. "On the first occasion that you saw Ramush Haradinaj at Jabllanice --"

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, forgive me, could I have one that's been paginated? Because I haven't got one, and everyone else seems to have got one. And it's a bit difficult for us to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course. We're printing one more. Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Can we print it and then see it, and then I can follow the argument and I can respond fairly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, Your Honour, on page 56: "On the first occasion that you saw Ramush Haradinaj at Jabllanice, which I understand was the occasion (redacted) (redacted), how was he being treated by other officers or commanders of the KLA? How were they treating him? "It was the first time for me to see him. They referred to him as commander, which means that he was protected by people who stood around him. He was so much protected, but there was very little of him I could see."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: (redacted). And when you look to the witness statement which Mr. Rogers wants to put to him, when you look to the witness statement Mr. Rogers wants to put to him, in that witness statement, at paragraphs 9 through to 15, he describes the ear-cutting incident in detail as having taken place on that very occasion, which is obviously different from the testimony he's given here. But the point is: You cannot use a witness statement to refresh a witness's memory about an event which is different in time from the one that he is now saying was the occasion on which the incident happened. He now says it happened (redacted). And when he has already said that he couldn't get a proper view of the person he said -- he was describing as Mr. Haradinaj, and now says that he can't be sure that the person -- Mr. Haradinaj was present. There's certainly not a foundation capable of being there. And whilst Mr. Rogers says the foundational questions haven't been asked, in fact they have been asked. They've been asked and answered by the witness. In relation to the second incident, Your Honours already have the point. In relation to the first incident, that is the point. And he's given an explanation in both cases, which makes memory refreshing impossible. We can deal with impeachment once Your Honours have ruled on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber will allow you to refresh the witness's memory on the ear-cutting incident where the witness says he doesn't remember. On the other one, the Chamber refuses your application, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask Your Honours that when the relevant passage is put to him, that it's put in full, from paragraphs 9 through, so that the context is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You will have an opportunity to do that, Mr. Emmerson, when you cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, with respect, it needs to be done now, as part of laying the foundation for memory refreshing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can Mr. Rogers conduct his prosecution of his case unassisted by the Defence, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, with respect - and perhaps we should just pause for a moment and take a breath - I have the right to make representations as to the manner in which the evidential foundation is properly to be laid in the course of memory refreshing. It would be unfair, and we would object to it, for you to permit the Prosecutor to selectively quote, unfairly and misleadingly and out of context, from the witness statement. I will object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, will you please object as and when the Prosecutor misquotes and selectively quotes. Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think we need the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session, if we are not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recall providing a witness statement to the Prosecution in (redacted)? You signed it in (redacted), but it was following on from interviews in (redacted). Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in (redacted). That's what you are asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Let me just show you a document. It's 65 ter 03046. And there should be an Albanian version with it. Do you see the Albanian version, Mr. Witness? Yes? I wonder if you could just -- in front of that green tab, you've got a green page there, on the left-hand side. On the other side is the signed version of the statement. Can you just see that? And have a look. And do you see what is page 12 of the statement? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is -- is that -- is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It appears so, but it seems rather different. But I don't understand. Can you please let me read it or tell me what is it -- what it is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes. I'll let you look at the -- the Albanian version in a moment. I just want to clarify the signatures. We see the date there the (redacted). Do you see that? And if you just turn --

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you just turn through the pages till you get to the front page, you'll see there are some initials on the bottom of each page on the left-hand side in the original signed version. That's it. Just turn it to the -- towards the front. Just turn each page over and look for the initials, would you? That's it. And do you see at the bottom there are some initials on each page? Can you see the initials?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And are those -- are those initials that you made and signed? Through the whole statement, from the back to the front, and look at each page to see if there are some initials. Can you confirm that the initials on those pages are yours and that you made them?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't know what to say. I have signed things, but I cannot say what you are asking me about. I want to know. Shouldn't simply stay here, but you should explain to me why, what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I just want to confirm with you that you signed a statement that you provided to the ICTY investigators in -- signed on the (redacted). I just want to ask you if you remember doing that, and the document that you have is a document that has your signature on it and is initialed by you on each page. Just confirm that you did provide that statement to the ICTY. I'll come and deal with the translation of it in a moment. But just can you confirm you did provide that written statement? [Microphone not activated] ... did provide the written statement?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave only an oral statement, not a written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Of the document that you have in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Could the bundle be given to me, please. Davor, could you just stay there with the witness. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm now showing you the first page, the front sheet of the statement. Can you see, at the bottom of it, a signature? Is your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). Do you see that? Is that a mark that you made? Initials -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: -- can you see the -- okay. Just turn over each page, please, and confirm that you initialed the bottom of each of those pages.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: When you get to that page, then stop. And you'll see your signature again in the middle and a date of the (redacted) -- (redacted); is that right? It's your signature and a date; is that right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Now just turn over till you get to the green page again, please. Keep going till you get to the green page. All right. Turn over the green page. What you're now looking at is a translation of the statement that you provided, which was originally in English, okay? So just have a look at the front page and you'll see all the details set out there of how and when the statement was taken. Just have a look at that. Just look at it and read it, that front page. Do you see there the details your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Rogers. May the Chamber please move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Court Officer. Yes, Mr. Rogers, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, on the front sheet there that you have translated, can we confirm that it contains your name, your date of birth, and information about when and where the interview took place?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And can you confirm that information as being correct, please.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at the time that you provided that statement, was your memory better about the events that took place in 1998 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a very long time has passed for me to remember everything. And knowing that, my situation, I told you on the first day that I'm not in a position to remember everything, because a long time has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Do --

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you should understand my predicament, that I am not in the situation I was 15 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, we understand that. But (redacted), when you were providing this statement, was your memory better then, do you think, than at the time you're giving your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But even at the time that I gave the statement I might have made some mistakes because I was under pressure, I was under threats. The gentleman who has taken this statement knows about the threats made against me. Some assassination attempts were staged against me. He knows very well. The police know that too. The Hague Tribunal know what I went through. I may have made some mistakes. Please explain to me where the problem lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Witness, let me take you -- I will explain where the problem lies. Can I take you to paragraph 15 of the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think we've got an answer to the critical memory-refreshing question, which is: Was your member better then than

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, were the events fresher in your memory in two-- in your mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think we got a clear answer. I think we got a clear answer in the first answer the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, the question was asked once and the answer was: A very long time has passed for me to remember. (redacted). The critical question on which any memory-refreshing exercise has to be founded is: Was your memory better at the time that the statement was made of those events or is it better now? And there's no necessary corollary merely from the chronological passage of time, because things may affect people's ability to remember, which pass with time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I heard an answer to that question, Mr. Emmerson. If you didn't, then we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... perhaps we can check the transcript. What was the answer again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could Your Honour indicate what answer it was you heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What was the answer? Sorry, I'm just trying to -- so that we can check the note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour indicated there was a clear answer. Might I inquire what Your Honour thinks the clear answer was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The clear answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour thinks the word "yes" is on the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What is it that Your Honour thinks was the clear answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't have the transcript before me, Mr. Emmerson -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I can get it to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- and I don't -- I don't want to go into this. This is my opinion -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sure Your Honour would like to check your recollection against the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: This is what I heard. No. No, I'm not a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, you're not a witness. But if you have a recollection, would you like to check it against the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we stop this, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm simply asking a question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Respectfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we stop this, Mr. Emmerson? Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I -- my submission is the question hasn't been answered. I would invite a ruling of the Chamber on that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And I understood. I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would invite a ruling of the Chamber on the question, not one member of the bench, and I'd like to have it done by reference to the transcript, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I think the question is whether the Bench is satisfied that the witness has provided an answer which indicates that his memory was different -- better then than it is now. Having regard to the totality of what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Judge Hall to respond on behalf of the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Moloto. As we understand the issue that is now in contention and which Mr. Emmerson raises, that is, the -- the necessity to have -- for there to be on the record a clear answer to the -- what is, in our view, the formal question as to whether the witness's memory was better at an earlier point in time when the statement on which the other side seeks to rely was better than it is now, and it is the Chamber's view that whatever answer the witness gives, it is -- whereas it may be -- form the foundation for future submissions, is not necessary to enable counsel who is relying on it to proceed. And in our view, Mr. Rogers may proceed and ask the question. Because the foundation, sufficient foundation, has been laid to put the -- to have the witness refresh his memory from the relevant paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, would you kindly turn to what is paragraph 15 of the Albanian version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I object, as I said I would, for it being taken out of context. It needs to be read from paragraph 9 onwards for the witness to be fairly asked questions about this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps this needs to be dealt with in the absence of the witness. I don't think we should be debating this in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're not going to do that, Mr. Rogers. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Mr. Emmerson will raise paragraph 9 when his time comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, look at paragraph 15, would you. And can you see -- just read that paragraph, if you would, to yourself. Don't read it out.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible to help me what is at issue in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes, I will. But I want you to read it first to yourself so that you have familiarized yourself with the content of that paragraph. And then I'll ask you my question. So just read it. Tell me when you finished reading it. Paragraph 15. It starts -- refers to a young boy. Do you see that? Something between 15 and 18. Just to make sure you're looking at the right paragraph. Have you -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found it. I don't know where it is. Is it possible that someone helps me to show where the paragraph is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... witness, are you able to find paragraph number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 15? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And are you able to read that paragraph in Albanian? Is it something you can read comfortably?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Now, do you see it refers to a young boy, something between 15 and 18. I just want to make sure you've got the right paragraph. Do you have that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I'm reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Read it to the end and tell me when you've got to the end, please. The end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, you'll recall that I asked you earlier whether you remembered whether Mr. Haradinaj was present during the course of that incident. Now you've had a chance to look at that paragraph, can you help, please, with whether you now recall whether Mr. Haradinaj was present during the course of that incident, now you've had a chance to read what you said (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier what I remember, that there are some things that I don't understand in detail. I know that Togeri was present in that incident; Idriz Balaj. As to Haradinaj, I said I don't recall. I recall that I have seen him several times, but I don't recall seeing him in this incident in question. I don't know why I gave this statement. When, sorry, I gave this ... I said that he was in that place several times. In that staff, I saw him, Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Just look, if you would, please, at the last -- the very last sentence of that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, that is the end of a memory-refreshing document. The witness has given his answer. This is now seeking to impeach the answer the witness has just given.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I haven't asked a question yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Overruled. Carry on, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Just have a look at that last sentence, if you would, please, of that paragraph, and see what you have said there (redacted).

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying it. Maybe I said it. I said that he has been there on several occasions, but -- but now I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, does that sentence, last sentence, not remind you of how you remembered things taking place at the time you wrote this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to the form of the question. The question isn't whether -- how he remembered things at the time of the statement. The question is, having seen the statement, whether he now remembers, having had his memory refreshed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Do you now remember, now that your memory has been refreshed, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said this before. At the time I was under pressure. I have given many statements. Now I don't remember that I have said it in this way. But now I'm telling the truth, that in some instances he has been there and that he was the commander of Dukagjin Plain. Haradin [as interpreted] was the commander. I am not saying that he was part of that massacre. I don't know that I have said that. I don't know why that is here. I am telling the truth, and so far I have been telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Answered. Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm conscious of the time, and I have to now deal with some of the other statements that he has made, and I may wish to make a further application, so -- but we're out of time for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are, indeed, out of time for now. I thought you made your application for two incidents and we said that we grant you the -- your application on the one incident and not on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But there may be--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you have further applications to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: There may be a further application I wish to make tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you so much. You may be seated. May the Chamber please move into closed session.
